description: Run an authorized shell script on an included free VM. Database commands are relayed through the included website VM. PostgreSQL is installed automatically; inspect before modifying it. Use get_free_resource_telemetry before builds and to diagnose resource pressure or failed services. Never print passwords or private keys. Inspect get_free_resource_action after scheduling, and preserve unknown outcomes without resubmitting. Use a service manager for long-running apps. Create application tables in database redu as role redu, never as postgres. For local administration use sudo -u postgres psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d redu and SET ROLE redu before application DDL or imports. This preserves console read/edit access and its default reader grants. A separate website runtime role may remain read-only. The default pg_hba.conf permits remote login only as redu from the website private address. For a separate runtime role, also add an exact host rule for database redu, that role and the website private IPv4 /32 with scram-sha-256 before the reject rules; validate pg_hba_file_rules and reload PostgreSQL. Keep all other sources rejected; never use trust or a public CIDR. Read the website address from the guest configuration rather than guessing it. SQL grants alone do not permit a new network login. Test the application connection from the website using its actual runtime role, without printing credentials, before publishing. If a shell command returns a nonzero exit code or the app returns HTTP 503, inspect its saved output and sanitized application error; do not repeat the installation blindly. Verify the table through postgres_data_read using the data-view ID returned by get_free_resources; discovery alone does not prove row access. Do not grant superuser or bypass row security to fix a permission error.

request_key.description: Stable request key. Reuse it after a timeout; never repeat an unknown command with a new key.

name: exec_free_resource
